animations.name: slow_rotation
animations.description: Full 360-degree Y-axis rotation revealing all three disulfide bonds and the compact hydrophobic core of this 46-residue plant seed protein.

animations.name: disulfide_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into the three disulfide bridges (Cys3-Cys40, Cys4-Cys32, Cys16-Cys26) that make crambin extraordinarily stable for its size.

animations.name: style_transition
animations.description: Morphs through four representation styles — VDW spheres to cartoon to sticks to hydrophobic surface — illustrating how protein visualization choices reveal different structural information.

transition_pairs.description: Protein-to-nucleic-acid contrast — compact folded chain dissolving into extended double helix.
Small stable protein expanding into GFP barrel — scale of fold complexity.

animations.name: helix_spin
animations.description: Top-down axial spin showing the 10.5 base-pair-per-turn B-form helix geometry and the major/minor groove width characteristic of canonical B-DNA.

animations.name: groove_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into the major groove where transcription factors bind, revealing the chemical readout surface — base-specific hydrogen bond donors and acceptors accessible without strand separation.

animations.name: base_pair_reveal
animations.description: Slow orbit while stepping through base pairs from 5' to 3' end, highlighting each Watson-Crick pair in sequence — CGCGAATTCGCG dodecamer showing AT-rich flexibility in the center.

transition_pairs.description: Free DNA expanding into CRISPR complex — naked duplex becoming guided-RNA-bound substrate.
DNA double helix acquiring p53 tetramer — transcription factor recognition event.

animations.name: t_to_r_state
animations.description: Simulates the T-state (tense, deoxy) to R-state (relaxed, oxy) quaternary conformational change — the alpha1-beta2 interface rotates 15 degrees, the basis of cooperative oxygen binding and the Bohr effect.

animations.name: heme_zoom
animations.description: Zooms from the tetrameric overview into a single heme group, revealing the porphyrin ring, the central iron atom, and the proximal histidine (His87) coordinating iron — the O2-binding site.

animations.name: symmetry_showcase
animations.description: Rotates through three principal axes to demonstrate the pseudo-D2 (222) symmetry of the alpha2-beta2 tetramer — two alpha and two beta subunits arranged around three mutually perpendicular 2-fold axes.

transition_pairs.description: Allosteric tetramer scaling up to rotary molecular machine — both use quaternary structure for cooperative function.
D2-symmetric tetramer dissolving into D3-symmetric insulin hexamer — contrasting oligomeric symmetry groups.

animations.name: central_axis_rotation
animations.description: Top-down axial view showing the F0 rotor c-ring (10-15 subunits depending on organism) spinning — the central gamma subunit rotates 120 degrees per ATP synthesized, driving conformational changes in each F1 beta subunit.

animations.name: stalk_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into the central stalk (gamma-delta-epsilon) that couples proton flow through F0 to ATP synthesis in F1 — the rotating axle at the heart of the chemiosmotic mechanism (Mitchell's Nobel prize).

animations.name: full_complex_reveal
animations.description: Slow orbit of the entire ~600 kDa complex from membrane-embedded F0 base through the peripheral stalk to the F1 catalytic head — the largest rotary molecular machine, ~8 nm tall.

transition_pairs.description: ATP synthase making ATP, then zooming to glutamine synthetase consuming ATP — both are large oligomeric nitrogen/energy metabolism machines.
Rotary machine scaling down to allosteric tetramer — contrasting mechanical vs. conformational mechanisms.

animations.name: dimer_symmetry
animations.description: Showcases the functional C2-symmetric homodimer — both active sites are exposed and catalytically competent only in the dimeric form, making dimer disruption a drug target strategy.

animations.name: active_site_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into the cysteine protease active site at the domain I-II cleft — the catalytic dyad (Cys145-His41) visible in stick representation, plus the oxyanion hole stabilizing the tetrahedral transition state. Target of Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir).

animations.name: inhibitor_highlight
animations.description: Transitions to surface hydrophobicity view of the active-site pocket, revealing the S1 (Glu166), S2, and S4 subsites that define substrate specificity for the Leu-Gln|Ser-Ala-Gly recognition sequence — basis for structure-based drug design.

transition_pairs.description: Two landmark COVID-era/CRISPR therapeutic targets — viral protease to bacterial endonuclease — the new era of precision medicine tools.
Cysteine protease to p53 tumor suppressor — two therapeutic targets of fundamentally different mechanism.

animations.name: barrel_spin
animations.description: Top-down view of the 11-strand beta-barrel spinning, showing the perfectly symmetric cylindrical fold that encloses and protects the chromophore — the 'lantern' architecture. The barrel shields the chromophore from solvent quenching.

animations.name: chromophore_zoom
animations.description: Dives through the beta barrel shell into the autocatalytically formed chromophore (Ser65-Tyr66-Gly67 cyclization) — the p-hydroxybenzylideneimidazolinone chromophore visible in ball-and-stick, the pi-conjugated system responsible for 488nm absorption and 507nm emission.

animations.name: surface_charge
animations.description: Transitions from rainbow cartoon to electrostatic surface to hydrophobic surface — revealing the charge distribution that governs GFP's behavior as a fusion tag in different cellular compartments.

transition_pairs.description: GFP (27 kDa) to crambin (4.7 kDa) — the most-used reporter shrinking to the smallest well-studied protein.
Monomeric GFP barrel expanding to hemoglobin tetramer — reporter protein meets oxygen carrier.

animations.name: d3_symmetry
animations.description: Top-down axial view showing the D3 (32) hexameric symmetry — three equivalent dimers arranged around a 3-fold axis, each dimer engaging a zinc ion at the center — the storage form in pancreatic beta-cell granules.

animations.name: zinc_site_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into the central zinc coordination site — two zinc ions each coordinated by three His10 residues from three chains in octahedral geometry — zinc is essential for hexamer stability during biosynthesis and pharmaceutical formulation.

animations.name: chain_reveal
animations.description: Orbits through all six chains (A1-B1, A2-B2, A3-B3) then reveals surface — emphasizing how three equivalent AB dimers assemble into the compact hexamer that enables slow-release pharmacokinetics in long-acting insulin formulations.

transition_pairs.description: D3 insulin hexamer to D2 hemoglobin tetramer — allosteric oxygen carrier vs. hormonal storage form.
Zinc-stabilized hexamer to dodecameric glutamine synthetase — two large oligomeric metabolic enzymes with central metal coordination.

animations.name: tetramer_on_dna
animations.description: Full orbit of the p53 tetramer wrapping around the response element DNA — two dimers bound to a 20-bp half-site each, the quarter-sites RRRCWWGYYY (R=purine, W=AT, Y=pyrimidine) recognized by the sequence-specific DNA-binding domain.

animations.name: dbd_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into the L3 loop and helix-turn-helix making sequence-specific contacts with the major groove — Arg248 and Arg273, two of the most frequently mutated hotspot residues in human cancer, visible inserting into the major groove.

animations.name: mutation_hotspot_highlight
animations.description: Zooms to the six hotspot mutation positions (R175H, G245S, R248W, R248Q, R249S, R273H) colored by B-factor flexibility — showing how cancer mutations cluster at the DNA-contact surface and metal-coordination site.

transition_pairs.description: p53 releasing DNA — protein dissociates to reveal free B-DNA, mimicking transcription factor unbinding.
Sequence-specific transcription factor to CRISPR guided endonuclease — two fundamentally different mechanisms of targeted DNA recognition.

animations.name: dodecamer_spin
animations.description: Top-down axial view of the D6h-symmetric dodecamer — two stacked hexameric rings with 6-fold symmetry — one of the largest and most symmetric metabolic enzymes, the central hub of nitrogen metabolism in all organisms.

animations.name: active_site_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into one of the 12 active sites at the interface between adjacent subunits in the same ring — the two Mn2+ ions visible coordinating glutamate and ATP for the glutamine + ADP + Pi synthesis reaction — a key antibiotic target.

animations.name: symmetry_showcase
animations.description: Slow orbit through all principal views revealing the stacked-ring dodecameric architecture — side view shows two hexameric discs, top view shows 6-fold symmetry, 45-degree view shows the interring contacts and the funnel-shaped active site pores.

transition_pairs.description: Glutamine synthetase consuming ATP to fix nitrogen, transitioning to ATP synthase making ATP — the nitrogen/energy cycle.
Dodecameric ring system contrasted with hexameric insulin — both use zinc-coordinated symmetry but at radically different scales.

animations.name: membrane_view_spin
animations.description: Top-down view through the lumen of the trimeric porin — three identical 16-strand beta-barrel channels visible as hollow cylinders, each ~7 Angstrom diameter at the eyelet — the size cutoff for passive diffusion of antibiotics and nutrients.

animations.name: channel_zoom
animations.description: Tilts to axial view and zooms into one beta-barrel channel, revealing the constriction zone (the 'eyelet') at half-membrane depth and the electrostatic potential surface — the alternating charged residues at the eyelet create the transverse electric field that drives cation selectivity.

animations.name: trimer_symmetry
animations.description: Rotating around the 3-fold symmetry axis of the trimer — showing how the three subunits associate via an extensive hydrophobic belt at the membrane-exposed surface, which is critical for correct outer membrane insertion by the BAM complex.

transition_pairs.description: Passive channel protein to active membrane-embedded rotary machine — both are integral outer/inner membrane proteins but radically different functional mechanisms.
Membrane-spanning protein trimer dissolving to expose the DNA strand inside — illustrating the range of structural biology targets.

animations.name: open_closed_morph
animations.description: Simulates the large-scale conformational change between open (apo) and closed (substrate-bound) states — the LID domain (residues 122-159) closes 20 Angstroms over the ATP binding site upon substrate binding, essential for the phosphoryl transfer reaction (ATP + AMP -> 2 ADP).

animations.name: active_site_zoom
animations.description: Zooms into the P-loop (phosphate binding loop, GXXXXGKS/T motif) and the Mg2+-ATP coordination — the catalytic mechanism requires the LID domain closing to exclude water, preventing futile ATP hydrolysis during the phosphoryl transfer.

animations.name: domain_highlight
animations.description: Steps through the three functional domains colored by B-factor: CORE (residues 1-29, 68-120, 160-214), LID (122-159), and AMPbind (30-67) — the high-B regions in LID and AMPbind correspond to the large-amplitude motions detected by NMR and single-molecule FRET.

transition_pairs.description: Adenylate kinase managing ATP/ADP/AMP equilibrium, transitioning to ATP synthase producing ATP — sequential steps in adenine nucleotide homeostasis.
Two enzymes with large conformational changes upon substrate binding — adenylate kinase and Mpro as examples of substrate-induced fit.

animations.name: guide_rna_zoom
animations.description: Zooms from the full 160 kDa complex into the seed region of the guide RNA:DNA heteroduplex — the 12 PAM-proximal base pairs whose complementarity is interrogated first — mismatch here aborts cleavage, explaining the specificity mechanism.

animations.name: nuclease_domains
animations.description: Slow orbit of the full Cas9-gRNA-DNA ternary complex, passing through views highlighting the RuvC and HNH nuclease domains (each cuts one strand) and the recognition lobe containing the PAM-interacting domain — the bilobed architecture apparent from every angle.

animations.name: pam_to_cut_site
animations.description: Zooms from the PAM recognition site (NGG read by Arg1333/Arg1335 in the PI domain) along the guide RNA-DNA hybrid toward the cleavage position 3 bp upstream of the PAM — the blunt-ended DSB created by HNH + RuvC acting on opposite strands.

transition_pairs.description: CRISPR complex releasing cleaved DNA — the severed duplex retreating from the guide RNA, mimicking product release after double-strand break.
CRISPR RNA-guided targeting vs. p53 protein sequence recognition — two entirely different molecular strategies for finding a specific genomic locus.
